title: Genomic prospecting and biochemical characterization of a novel thermostable 3-quinuclidinone reductase from hot spring metagenomes for efficient biocatalysis.
authors: Lou, Deshuai; Cui, Jinghao; Duan, Jingfa; Zhou, Bingpu; Wang, Yue; Wang, Dong; Tan, Jun; Duan, Hongtao
one_liner_zh: 该文从热泉宏基因组发现新型耐热3-奎宁环酮还原酶，结合MD模拟与LigandMPNN/UniKP结构导向设计优化其催化性能，属于蛋白质结构计算与设计在酶工程中的应用，方法创新有限但对象、问题、方法均相关。
abstract: This study presents the discovery and characterization of a novel thermophilic 3-quinuclidinone reductase (ScQR) identified through metagenomic mining of hot spring environments. ScQR, a member of the short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase (SDR) superfamily, was heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli, and its catalytic properties were systematically characterized. The enzyme demonstrates exceptional thermal stability, retaining 86% of its activity after 48 hours at 70 degrees C. Furthermore, K(+) and Mg(2)(+) ions significantly enhanced ScQR's activity at specific concentrations. Structural analysis revealed that ScQR adopts a typical SDR fold with a conserved catalytic triad (S141-Y155-K159), and it is NAD(H) dependent. Enzyme assays indicated that ScQR is highly stereoselective for (R)-3-quinuclidinol, with no activity against its enantiomer, (S)-3-quinuclidinol. The enzyme exhibits optimal activity at pH 9 and 85 degrees C, making it a promising candidate for industrial applications requiring high thermal stability. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed that ScQR preserves global structural integrity up to 360 K, whereas higher temperatures induce destabilization, predominantly in the C-terminal region and residues 95-100. In addition, structure-guided computational design enabled by LigandMPNN and UniKP yielded three ScQR variants with improved substrate affinity and catalytic efficiency while maintaining the overall fold and function. This work underscores the power of metagenomics with structure-driven protein design in discovering novel enzymes with unique catalytic properties from extreme environments and establishes ScQR as a promising biocatalyst for biotechnological and pharmaceutical applications.IMPORTANCEThis study reports the discovery of ScQR, a novel thermophilic 3-quinuclidinone reductase identified via metagenomic mining. ScQR represents one of the most heat-resistant members of the SDR superfamily discovered to date, maintaining 86% activity after 48 hours at 70 degrees C. These findings establish ScQR as a robust biocatalyst for high-temperature pharmaceutical applications and demonstrate a scalable workflow for optimizing enzymes from extreme environments, offering significant value to the fields of biocatalysis and protein engineering.
abstract_zh:
本研究报道了一种新型嗜热3-奎宁环酮还原酶（ScQR）的发现与表征，该酶通过温泉环境宏基因组挖掘鉴定获得。ScQR属于短链脱氢酶/还原酶（SDR）超家族，在大肠杆菌中异源表达，并对其催化性质进行了系统表征。该酶表现出卓越的热稳定性，在70摄氏度下孵育48小时后仍保留86%的活性。此外，K(+)和Mg(2)(+)离子在特定浓度下显著增强了ScQR的活性。结构分析显示，ScQR采用典型的SDR折叠，具有保守的催化三联体（S141-Y155-K159），且依赖NAD(H)。酶活性测定表明，ScQR对(R)-3-奎宁环醇具有高度立体选择性，而对其对映体(S)-3-奎宁环醇无活性。该酶在pH 9和85摄氏度下表现出最佳活性，使其成为需要高热稳定性的工业应用的有前景候选酶。分子动力学模拟进一步揭示，ScQR在高达360 K时保持整体结构完整性，而更高温度主要诱导C末端区域和残基95-100的不稳定化。此外，通过LigandMPNN和UniKP实现的结构引导计算设计产生了三个ScQR变体，这些变体在保持整体折叠和功能的同时，提高了底物亲和力和催化效率。本研究强调了宏基因组学与结构驱动蛋白设计相结合在从极端环境中发现具有独特催化性质的新型酶方面的强大能力，并将ScQR确立为生物技术和制药应用中有前景的生物催化剂。

重要性本研究报道了通过宏基因组挖掘发现的ScQR——一种新型嗜热3-奎宁环酮还原酶。ScQR代表了迄今为止发现的SDR超家族中最耐热的成员之一，在70摄氏度下48小时后仍保持86%的活性。这些发现将ScQR确立为高温制药应用中稳健的生物催化剂，并展示了一种从极端环境中优化酶的可扩展工作流程，为生物催化和蛋白质工程领域提供了重要价值。
